get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of purchase debit notes for the account. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. It requires the **Inventory** plugin to be active.

A purchase debit note is a purchase document that shares storage with purchase orders and is identified by its document type. This endpoint returns only debit-note records.

### Data-level path segment

The trailing path segment (`-1`) is the **relation data level** — how deeply related records are eager-loaded — not a page number. Use `-1` (load base record with light relations only). Calling the list **without** a data level (`.../purchase_debit_note/list`) attempts to eager-load the full relation graph and fails with a `400` database error, so always include the segment.

### Pagination & query parameters

| Parameter | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `page` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `per_page` | Items per page (default `20`). |
| `filter[<field>]` | Filter by a field's value, e.g. `filter[no]=PDN-0001` or `filter[supplier_id]=1`. |
| `sort[<field>]` | Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[date]=desc`. Default ordering is newest first (`id` descending). |
| `version` | Set to `2` to run each row through the listing formatter (adds display-formatted values); the top-level envelope is unchanged. |

**Filterable fields.** Filter with `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>` (the operator is optional; `filter[<field>]=<value>` uses a default match). The fields intended for filtering:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `no` | string | `filter[no]=PDN-0001` |
| `supplier_id` | integer (supplier) | `filter[supplier_id]=1` |
| `date` | date | `filter[date][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01` |
| `summary_total` | number | `filter[summary_total][greater_than_equal]=100` |
| `tags` | string | `filter[tags]=urgent` |

**Sortable fields.** Sort with `sort[<field>]=asc|desc`. The fields intended for sorting:

| Field | Type | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `date` | date | `sort[date]=desc` |
| `no` | string | `sort[no]=asc` |
| `created` | datetime | `sort[created]=desc` |

The API will in fact filter and sort on any existing column of the record; the tables above list the fields the product surfaces for this entity. With no `sort`, results are ordered by `id` descending.

### Response

The response is a standard paginated envelope (`current_page`, `data`, `per_page`, `total`, `last_page`, and the page-URL/link fields). Each item in `data` is a flat purchase debit note record.

`payment_status` and `requisition_delivery_status` are returned as codes; their meanings are listed on those fields below.

parameters.description: Relation eager-loading depth. Use `-1` (base record with light relations only). Omitting the segment entirely (`.../list`) attempts to load the full relation graph and fails with a `400` database error, so a value is required.

parameters.description: Page number. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Items per page. Defaults to `20`.

parameters.name: filter[<field>]
parameters.description: Filter results by a field's value, e.g. `filter[no]=PDN-0001` or `filter[supplier_id]=1`. An operator can be added as `filter[<field>][<operator>]=<value>` (e.g. `filter[date][greater_than_equal]=2026-01-01`). Fields intended for filtering: `no`, `supplier_id`, `date`, `summary_total`, `tags`.

parameters.name: sort[<field>]
parameters.description: Sort by a field, `asc` or `desc`, e.g. `sort[date]=desc`. Fields intended for sorting: `date`, `no`, `created`. Default ordering is `id` descending.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Set to `2` to run each row through the listing formatter (adds display-formatted values). The top-level envelope is unchanged.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a purchase debit note. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token. It requires the **Inventory** plugin to be active.

A purchase debit note shares storage with purchase orders and is identified by its document type, so **`type` must be `14`** — sending a different type (or omitting it) fails with a `400` (`"error": "Record Not Found"`) because the entity can only be resolved for type `14`.

### Request body

The body is a flat JSON object. The account layer enforces exactly three required fields — omitting any of them returns `422`:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `supplier_business_name` | Required, non-empty. |
| `draft` | Required. `1` = save as draft, `0` = finalized. |
| `summary_total.currency` | Required, non-empty (the currency of the totals object). |

In addition, `type` must be `14` for the record to save (enforced below the validation layer with a `400`).

All other fields are optional. `no` (the debit-note number) is generated automatically when omitted. `currency_code` and `supplier_id` are optional. Server-managed fields (`id`, `created`, `modified`, `branch_id`, `site_id`, `staff_id`, payment/summary totals) are assigned by the server.

### Line items

Line items are sent under the **`purchase_debit_notes_items`** array (each entry becomes a purchase-order-item row). Each item takes `product_id`, `item` (name), `description`, `unit_price`, `quantity`, `discount`, `discount_type`, `tax1`, `tax2`, and optional `col_3`..`col_5` extra columns.

### Statuses

`requisition_delivery_status`:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Received |
| 2 | Rejected |
| 3 | Pending |
| 4 | Partially Received |
| 5 | Partially Rejected |

On success the response is `{ "message": "...", "id": <new id> }`; the message is localized to the caller's language.

draft.description:
Required. Whether to save the document as a draft.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Draft |
| 0 | Finalized |

type.description: Required. Document type. Must be `14` (purchase debit note); any other value returns a `400` (`Record Not Found`).

currency.description: Required, non-empty. Currency code of the totals (e.g. `EGP`).

currency_code.description: Optional. Currency code of the document (e.g. `EGP`).

no.description: Optional. Debit-note number. Generated automatically when omitted.

staff_id.description: Optional. Id of the staff member. Defaults to the authenticated user.

work_order_id.description: Optional. Id of a linked work order.

requisition_delivery_status.description:
Optional. Requisition delivery status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Received |
| 2 | Rejected |
| 3 | Pending |
| 4 | Partially Received |
| 5 | Partially Rejected |

tags.description: Optional. Tags to assign to the document.

purchase_debit_notes_items.description: Line items. Each entry is persisted as a purchase-order-item row.

discount_type.description:
Discount type.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Percentage |
| 2 | Fixed amount |

tax1.description: Id of the first tax applied to the item, or null.

tax2.description: Id of the second tax applied to the item, or null.

200.description: The purchase debit note was created.

id.description: Id of the newly created purchase debit note.

400.description: The record passed validation but could not be saved — most commonly because `type` was missing or not `14` (`"error": "Record Not Found"`).

e.description: Error detail (an object for database-level failures, or an empty array for other save failures).

error.description: Reason the record could not be saved. `Record Not Found` is returned when `type` is missing or not `14`.

401.description: The Bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired.

422.description: A required field failed validation. `errors` maps each failing field (`supplier_business_name`, `draft`, `summary_total.currency`) to its messages.

errors.description: Map of field name to an array of error messages. Returned when `supplier_business_name`, `draft`, or `summary_total.currency` is missing or empty.

post.description: MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a purchase refund (purchase debit note). The request must include a `PurchaseRefund` object and at least one `PurchaseOrderItem`. Required: `PurchaseRefund.supplier_id`; each item requires `item`, `unit_price`, and `quantity`. Set `PurchaseRefund.subscription_id` to the id of the purchase invoice being refunded to link the refund to its source invoice; omit it to create a standalone refund. `currency_code`, the refund number, store, branch, and totals are assigned automatically when omitted. Send `?send=draft` to save as a draft (otherwise the refund is marked received). Requires the Inventory plugin and the *Add New Purchase Orders* permission.

parameters.name: send
parameters.description: Set to `draft` to save the refund as a draft instead of a received refund.

id.description: Identifier of the newly created purchase refund.

message.description: Set for business-rule failures (e.g. source purchase invoice not found, supplier suspended, insufficient stock when over-draft is disabled). `validation_errors` is populated for field validation failures.

get.description: Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a single purchase refund (purchase debit note) by id, including its line items, payments, taxes, and supplier details. Requires the Inventory plugin to be active.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The purchase refund id.

put.description: MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing purchase refund (purchase debit note). The request must include a `PurchaseRefund` object and at least one `PurchaseOrderItem`. Required: `PurchaseRefund.supplier_id`; each item requires `item`, `unit_price`, and `quantity`. The line items sent replace the existing ones. Payments are NOT accepted on update (this route accepts only `PurchaseRefund` and `PurchaseOrderItem`). Send `?send=draft` to keep the refund as a draft. Requires the Inventory plugin and an Edit/Delete Purchase Orders permission.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The purchase refund id.

parameters.name: send
parameters.description: Set to `draft` to keep the refund as a draft instead of a received refund.

message.description: Set for business-rule failures (e.g. insufficient stock when over-draft is disabled). `validation_errors` is populated for field validation failures.

delete.description: MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Deletes a purchase refund (purchase debit note) by id. The refund cannot be deleted when it has an accepted or modified requisition, when its requisition is already received, when it has linked refunds/credit/debit notes, or when over-draft is disabled and the items already have stock transactions. Deleting also reverses its stock transactions, journals, and supplier balance. Requires the Inventory plugin and an Edit/Delete Purchase Orders permission.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The purchase refund id.

message.description: Returned for: insufficient delete permission; a missing or invalid id; a requisition that is already received; linked refunds/credit notes/debit notes; or items that already have stock transactions when over-draft is disabled.
Returned when the refund has an accepted or modified requisition and cannot be deleted.

get.description: Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a single purchase invoice by its identifier, including its line items, supplier, taxes, custom fields, and payments. Only records of type purchase invoice are returned; other document types yield 404.

Required: `PurchaseOrder.supplier_id`; each `PurchaseOrderItem` requires `item`, `unit_price`, and `quantity`. Custom-field values may be sent; payments are NOT accepted on update (use the payments endpoints). An invoice created from a purchase order can only be edited with the appropriate approval permission. The same operation is also available via `POST /purchase_invoices/{id}`.

delete.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. **Not currently available.** Although this route is registered, deleting a purchase order through the legacy REST API is not implemented: the request always returns an HTTP **404** with `{ "result": "failed", "code": 404, "message": "Invalid Endpoint" }` and no purchase order is deleted.

To delete a purchase order, use the v2 entity API for the `purchase_order` entity.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The purchase order id.

404.description: This endpoint is not currently available and always returns a 404 "Invalid Endpoint" error. No purchase order is deleted. Delete purchase orders through the v2 entity API instead.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Legacy compatibility endpoint for listing purchase orders.

This endpoint does **not** return a JSON collection. It responds with an HTTP **302** redirect whose `Location` header points to the v2 entity listing for purchase orders (`/v2/owner/entity/purchase_order-13/list`). To retrieve the purchase-order collection — with pagination, search and filtering — call the v2 entity listing endpoint for the `purchase_order` entity. Use `GET /purchase_orders/{id}` to fetch a single purchase order as JSON.

302.description: The legacy list endpoint responds with an HTTP 302 redirect to the v2 entity listing for purchase orders. No JSON collection is returned by this endpoint itself.

Location.description: The v2 entity listing URL for purchase orders that the request is redirected to.

401.description: Returned when the access token is missing or invalid.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a new purchase order.

Send a `PurchaseOrder` object together with a `PurchaseOrderItem` array; optionally include a `Payment` object to record an immediate payment and a `PurchaseOrderCustomField` array. The only hard-required fields are `PurchaseOrder.supplier_id` and, for each line item, `item`, `quantity` and `unit_price`; most other fields are defaulted automatically (currency, date, number, store, branch).

The document `type` and `payment_status` are set server-side and any client values for them are ignored. Whether the order is saved as a draft is controlled by the `send` query parameter, not a body field.

On success the endpoint returns HTTP **202** with `{ "result": "successful", "code": 202, "id": <new id> }`.

parameters.name: send
parameters.description:
Optional save/send behaviour.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| draft | Save the purchase order as a draft (no number is assigned yet) |
| direct | Save and email it to the supplier |
| revised | Save and open the send-to-supplier flow |
| print | Save and prepare a printable copy |

Omit to save a normal (issued) purchase order.

supplier_id.description: Required. The supplier this order is placed with; must reference an existing supplier.

currency_code.description: Optional. ISO currency code (e.g. `USD`). Defaults to the account currency when omitted.

date.description: Optional. Order date in the account date format. Defaults to today.

issue_date.description: Optional. Issue date in the account date format.

supplier_email.description: Required only when the supplier's invoicing method is email; must be a valid email address.

discount_amount.description: Optional. Order-level discount as a fixed amount (≥ 0).

store_id.description: Optional. Destination store/warehouse; must be active.

PurchaseOrderItem.description: Line items. At least one item is expected; each item requires `item`, `quantity` and `unit_price`.

product_id.description: Optional. Linked product id; the product must be active.

tax.description:
Optional. Tax mode.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | No taxes |
| 1 | Tax 1 |
| 2 | Tax 2 |
| 3 | Both taxes |

store_id.description: Optional. Per-item store; must be active.

Payment.description: Optional. Record an immediate payment against the order.

treasury_id.description: Treasury to deposit into. Defaults to the primary treasury when omitted.

currency_code.description: Defaults to the purchase order's currency when omitted.

202.description: Purchase order created. The body carries the new purchase order id only.

id.description: The id of the newly created purchase order.

400.description: Validation failed, or a referenced product/store is inactive, or the order could not be created.

validation_errors.description: Field-keyed validation messages, present when validation fails.

403.description: The authenticated staff member lacks the Manage Purchase Orders permission.

get.description:
Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a single purchase order as JSON, identified by its id. Only records of type Purchase Order are returned by this endpoint.

The purchase order's line items, supplier, creating staff member, custom fields, attachments, taxes and payments are nested **inside** the `data.PurchaseOrder` object (e.g. `data.PurchaseOrder.PurchaseOrderItem`). The `password` field is omitted from the nested `Supplier` and `Staff` objects.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The purchase order id.

PurchaseOrder.description: The purchase order record. Included relations are nested inside this object.

is_received.description: Delivery/receipt status. `0` Unreceived, `1` Received, `2`/`4` Partially Received, `3` Under Delivery, `-1` Draft.

payment_status.description: `0` Unpaid, `1` Partially Paid, `2` Paid, `3` Refunded, `4` Overpaid, `-1` Draft.

Staff.description: Creating staff record (the `password` field is omitted).

403.description: The authenticated staff member lacks permission to view this purchase order.

404.description: No purchase order with this id exists (or it is not a Purchase Order record).

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing purchase order.

Send the `PurchaseOrder` header object plus the full `PurchaseOrderItem` array (the supplied items replace the existing ones); optionally include `PurchaseOrderCustomField`. The `id` comes from the path. The only hard-required fields are `PurchaseOrder.supplier_id` and, per line item, `item`, `quantity` and `unit_price`. The document `type` is set server-side.

**Response note:** a JSON success body (`{ "result": "successful", "code": 200 }`) is returned only when the `send=direct` query parameter is provided. Without it, a successful update responds with an HTTP 302 redirect to the v2 show page rather than a JSON body. Editing an order that has already been invoiced returns a 400 error.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The purchase order id to update.

parameters.name: send
parameters.description:
Optional save/send behaviour. **Pass `direct` to receive a JSON success acknowledgement** — without it, a successful update responds with an HTTP 302 redirect instead of a JSON body.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| direct | Save, email the supplier, and return a JSON success body |
| revised | Save and open the send-to-supplier flow |
| print | Save and prepare a printable copy |
| draft | Save as a draft |

PurchaseOrder.description: The purchase order header fields to update. The `id` is taken from the path.

supplier_id.description: Required. Must reference an existing supplier.

date.description: Optional. Order date in the account date format.

supplier_email.description: Required when the supplier's invoicing method is email; must be a valid email.

PurchaseOrderItem.description: The full set of line items for the order (replaces the existing items). Each item requires `item`, `quantity` and `unit_price`.

id.description: Optional. Existing line item id to update; omit for new items.

product_id.description: Optional. Linked product id; the product must be active.

tax.description:
Optional. Tax mode.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | No taxes |
| 1 | Tax 1 |
| 2 | Tax 2 |
| 3 | Both taxes |

store_id.description: Optional. Per-item store; must be active.

200.description: Purchase order updated. Returned as a JSON body only when the `send=direct` query parameter is supplied; otherwise a successful update responds with an HTTP 302 redirect to the v2 show page.

400.description: The order is already invoiced, a referenced product/store is inactive, or validation failed.

validation_errors.description: Field-keyed validation messages, present when validation fails.

403.description: The staff member lacks the Manage Purchase Orders permission, or the order originates from a purchase quotation and the caller lacks approval permission.

404.description: No purchase order with this id exists.
